Julia / Aditya — hi. Below are the technical answers and pointers to the artifacts we'll attach. I kept items grouped by deployment mode as you requested.

1) RTO / RPO
- Hosted API (Redwood Managed):
  - RTO target: 1 hour for sustained regional outage with automated routing to warm-standby region (typical path: capacity shift + cache rebuild).
  - RPO target: < 15 minutes for persistent storage (transactional logs and snapshots). KV-caches are best-effort; we replay in-flight context when available.
- Dedicated (Reserved GPU Pools):
  - RTO target: 2 hours for cross-region failover to a warm pool allocated in standby region.
  - RPO target: < 30 minutes for model state and persistent stores.
- Private (VPC / On-prem):
  - RTO/RPO are customer-configurable. Typical default config we ship: RTO 4 hours, RPO 1 hour for customer-managed private deployments. With customer-managed warm standby and networking pre-provisioned we can reduce these to Hosted-like numbers.

2) Backups & Retention
- Snapshot cadence: persistent volumes are snapshotted every 4 hours; incremental snapshots hourly for workloads with high write volume.
- Full backups: nightly full snapshot of model artifacts and metadata.
- Retention: default 90 days for snapshots; long-term retention (archival) configurable up to 1 year or longer via export.
- Offsite replication: snapshots replicated asynchronously to at least one paired region (us-west-2 <-> us-east-1 for US customers) within the snapshot window.

3) Failover behavior
- Automated routing: control-plane detects regional health signals and initiates traffic routing to warm standby region when latency/error thresholds exceed SLOs. Warm standby has pre-provisioned model instances and pre-warmed caches (where policy allows).
- Manual elevation: for Private deployments and some Dedicated contracts we require manual cutover for targeted data-sync verification. Manual procedure is documented in the runbook.
- Expected service restoration: when automated failover completes we verify model inference correctness and replay any transient request context where possible. For Hosted we aim to restore full API functionality within the RTO window above.

4) KMS & encryption
- All snapshots and persistent volumes are encrypted at rest using AWS KMS (or equivalent cloud provider KMS).
- For Private installations we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and BYOK flows.
- Audit/KMS logs: we record key usage and vault access in our audit pipeline and can export logs for a specified date range.

5) DR testing cadence and evidence
- We run full DR rehearsals quarterly for the core control plane and semi-annually for model-serving stacks; targeted tests are run after major infra changes.
- Latest test: 2026-09-30 (attached summary), outcome: automated failover validated for a simulated us-west-2 region outage, RTO met (1h) for Hosted path, and Dedicated failover validated with manual cutover (2h).

Artifacts to be attached in the next message: runbook PDF, DR test summary CSV, snapshot policy export. If you need a redacted export or a sample KMS log export, indicate the date range and whether you need platform-wide or tenant-scoped records.

Happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk through the runbook.

--
Evelyn Hart
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Quick summary (high level):
- Hosted: RTO 1h / RPO <15m; automatic failover to warm standby region; snapshots every 4h; retention 90 days.
- Dedicated: RTO 2h / RPO <30m; cross-region warm pools; manual cutover documented when DB sync needed.
- Private: default template RTO 4h / RPO 1h; supports CMKs and BYOK; customers can opt for tighter SLAs.
- KMS: snapshots encrypted at rest; audit logs available and can be exported (specify dates).
